decision: Keep the supplied train and test files separate
reason: I wanted to preserve the chronological hold-out design.

decision: Do not load the official test file before model freezing
reason: I wanted to protect the independence of my final test evaluation.
I wanted the models to learn transaction behaviour rather than customer identity.
I did not assume that one imbalance method would always be best.

decision: Apply sampling only inside model pipelines
reason: I wanted to reduce the risk of data leakage.
I wanted a fair comparison between the supervised algorithms.

decision: Reject tuning if PR-AUC becomes worse
reason: I did not want tuning to automatically replace a stronger original model.

decision: Choose the final model using chronological validation
reason: I wanted model selection to happen before opening the test dataset.

decision: Use the same fitted validation model for final test evaluation
reason: I wanted the selected threshold to remain consistent with the exact fitted model.
I wanted to test whether my engineered features actually added predictive value.

decision: Use fraud risk score rather than fraud probability
reason: I do not claim that the raw classifier score is a calibrated banking probability.
I wanted to show uncertainty around my final model metrics.
I wanted to understand where my selected model still makes mistakes.
